name: heatsink_natural_mlp
description: PINNeAPPle ModelRegistry 'bench_mlp' (4 x 128, SiLU) on log-scaled geometry, material and operating variables, trained on 5000 solves of the HeatSink Sizer physics engine in natural convection (Bar-Cohen & Rohsenow composite correlation, 3-D finite-volume base conduction) with monotonicity constraints: a hinge penalty keeps d log R / d log k and d log R / d log(source width) negative on the training designs and on random in-range designs (pinneapple_design.thermal.heatsink.monotone). Returns the resistance and a split-conformal 95 % upper bound.
task: Plate-fin heat sink in natural convection (vertical fins, free air): base-to-air thermal resistance

outputs.name: r_base_k_w
outputs.description: thermal resistance, base to ambient air

validity_range.fin_gap_note: gap sampled in 2.5-20 mm, then the fin count is rounded; the realised gaps of the training designs span 2.2-30.6 mm
validity_range.regime: natural convection in free air, vertical fins, no radiation

known_limitations: Natural convection without radiation: at low power, radiation can carry a comparable share of the heat for black-anodised sinks; the reference does not model it.
Correlation-based reference (typical +-15 % against experiments); the surrogate's own error is against the engine, not against a measurement.
The engine's resistance rises with power on 0.5 % of designs (non-monotone correlation blending); the power law is checked on the model but not enforced in training.
Screening tool: re-verify a chosen design with the physics engine.
equations: Bar-Cohen & Rohsenow (1984) composite natural-convection correlation for vertical parallel plates
3-D finite-volume conduction in the base (spreading resistance)

training_config.optimizer: library Trainer, Adam lr 2e-3, batch 128, best-val checkpoint: 50 epochs of plain regression, then 550 epochs with the hinge penalty (weight 100, margin 5e-4 in d log R / d log x); then 4 rounds of full-batch L-BFGS on the same constrained objective

reference_source: 750 held-out designs solved by the HeatSink Sizer physics engine (pinneapple_design.thermal.heatsink.engine). The engine is checked against independent methods: natural h vs Elenbaas (1942) 2 %, Lee et al. spreading (1-5 %), FVM grid convergence < 2 %.
citation: PINNeAPPle contributors (2026). HeatSink Sizer natural-convection surrogate (monotone). PINNeAPPle model zoo, https://github.com/PINNeAPPle-Labs/PINNeAPPle

checagens.name: card metrics reproduced on the stored reference (max relative difference)
checagens.source: 750 held-out designs solved by the HeatSink Sizer physics engine (pinneapple_design.thermal.heatsink.engine). The engine

checagens.name: held-out test/R_mean_abs_pct within the zoo acceptance limit
held-out test/R_p95_abs_pct within the zoo acceptance limit
monotonic: a more conductive material never raises the resistance (share of held-out designs violating, +5 % step)
monotonic: a wider heat source spreads less (lower resistance) (share of held-out designs violating, +5 % step)
monotonic: more power drives more buoyant flow (lower resistance) (share of held-out designs violating, +5 % step)
checagens.source: natural convection, h ~ dT^(1/4); the engine itself violates it on 0.5 % of designs
